title: PSOE Audit & Surveillance (CAAN Appendix 10)
subtitle: Provider Surveillance & Oversight Evaluation
overview: PSOE audits evaluate a provider's SMS against the standard surveillance checklist in the CAAN SMS Procedure Manual, Appendix 10 (ICAO Annex 19 aligned).

The checklist is organised into the four SMS components. Each surveillance question is scored 0-3 on the implementation scale; questions that do not apply to the provider are marked N/A and excluded from the score.

method.title: Method & Scoring Rules
paragraphs: Four components with fixed weights — Safety Policy & Objectives 10%, Safety Risk Management 40%, Safety Assurance 30%, Safety Promotion 20%.
Scoring scale — 0: Not Implemented / Non-Compliant; 1: Partially Implemented (Documented only); 2: Implemented & Operational; 3: Fully Effective & Continuous Improvement.
N/A handling — a Not-Applicable answer is excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, so it cannot drag the score down.
Overall score — each component is scored as a percentage of applicable questions, then combined using the component weights.
bullets: Target thresholds — ≥90% Fully Effective & Continuous Improvement; ≥70% Implemented & Operational; ≥40% Partially Implemented (Documented only); below 40% Not Implemented / Non-Compliant.
A draft assessment can be saved with partial responses; scores are recomputed whenever responses change.
The template, weights, and target thresholds are versioned so older assessments stay reproducible.

mapping.title: CAR-19 / Appendix 10 Mapping
paragraphs: The four components map directly to ICAO Annex 19 safety management pillars.
Safety Risk Management carries the highest weight (40%) because hazard identification, risk assessment and mitigation are the core of an effective SMS under CAR-19.

example.title: Worked Example
paragraphs: A provider is assessed across all four components (all questions applicable).
Safety Policy & Objectives scored 100%, Safety Risk Management 60%, Safety Assurance 80%, Safety Promotion 90%.
If a question were not applicable (e.g. no Part-145 activity), it would be marked N/A and simply excluded from its component's denominator.
